violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Debris observed on the interior front panel of the ice machine and not being cleaned as required in the back kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: overfilled metal container of deli sliced provolone cheese stored improperly made icebath on prep counter near flatgrill on front cookline. EHS observed top slices of stacked provolone cheese with ambient temperature of 56F. EHS observed metal pan too big to be properly stored in ice bath and allow ice to cover all areas of the metal container storing the provolone cheese.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated the top stack of the deli sliced provolone cheese to another pan and relocated to inside the True 3 Dr UR refrigerator to cool to at least 41F or below. CFM placed metal container of deli sliced provolone to a bigger container of ice where all sides are sufficiently covered with ice and able to maintain at least 41F or below.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: multiple overfilled metal containers of recently sliced tomatoes (47F, 49F) cooling in the top and bottom of the Migali 3 Dr preptop refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: CFM portioned half of the sliced tomatoes in another metal container and True 3 Dr UR refrigerator in the back kitchen area to rapidly cool tomatoes to at least 41F or below before being relocated back to front cold hold units. Blessing Cafe (Inspection Date: 08/17/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Thermometers, Location in Holding Units
violations.observation: The temperature measuring device in the following mechanically refrigerated unit was not properly located in the warmest part of the unit: Delfield 1 Dr UC refrigerator (front prep area). EHS observed high temperature dial thermometer with starting temperature of 100F being used as ambient thermometer in unit.
violations.corrective_action: In a mechanically refrigerated unit the sensor of a temperature measuring device shall be located to measure the air temperature of a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of the refrigerator. Store the thermometer near the door of the unit. EHS instructed CFM to place ambient thermometer capable of reading low temperatures inside the Delfield 1 Dr UC refrigerator to ensure the unit is maintaining an ambient temperature of at least 41F or below.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location. Permit is posted in back kitchen prep area.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. EHS instructed CFM to relocate to conspicuous location in the front area that is visible to customers.

violations.observation: Box of tomatoes stored directly in front of hand sink in back kitchen area where it is subject to possible splashing from water when employees wash hands.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. CDI: CFM relocated tomatoes to area away from hand sink.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS emailed CFM copy of written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events and CFM ordered bodily fluid cleanup kit.

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): rice is being held below 135 for three hours as stated by manager, no TPHC policy in place, food is not marked for time tracking.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. Inspector provided link to TPHC documents. Rice must be marked according to the policy.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: sesame oil held in opaque red squeeze bottle, gochujang sauce Lao held in red squeeze bottles.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc.
